findings.excerpt: carrier := {p | ∀ α i, m.degree (b i) ≤ α → p.coeff α = 0}
findings.problem: `reducedSubmodule` is a hand-built R-submodule of `MvPolynomial σ R` whose elements are the polynomials supported on a given set of exponents, namely those not above any `m.degree (b i)`. Mathlib already has `MvPolynomial.restrictSupport R s`, the submodule of polynomials with support in `s`, together with `mem_restrictSupport_iff`, `restrictSupport_mono`, `restrictSupport_eq_span` and a basis. The file re-proves zero, add and smul closure by hand, and its membership predicate (`∀ α i, … → coeff α = 0`) is a differently shaped restatement of `↑p.support ⊆ s`. As a result, `reducedSubmodule` cannot use the existing support-restriction API. Reduced remainders are also stated as `∀ α ∈ support, ∀ i, ¬ …` (as in Mathlib's `MonomialOrder.div`), which is the `restrictSupport` form and not the `reducedSubmodule` form. `basisDivision_reduced` and `linearDivision_remainder_support` therefore convert between the two forms.
findings.proposed_change: Drop the structure-based definition. Either define `reducedSubmodule m b := restrictSupport R {α | ∀ i, ¬ m.degree (b i) ≤ α}` as an abbreviation, or use that `restrictSupport` term directly. Then `mem_restrictSupport_iff` gives the support statement directly, with no coeff/support conversion. `basisDivision_reduced` follows from the `∀ β ∈ support, …` clause in `basisDivision`. The `Submodule.sum_mem` argument in `linearDivision_remainder_support` can stay but uses `restrictSupport`'s own closure. The hand-written closure proofs can be deleted.
findings.benefit: This removes a duplicate submodule definition and its three closure proofs. It aligns the reduced-remainder condition with the support form Mathlib's `div` already uses. It also lets users apply existing `restrictSupport` lemmas (monotonicity, span, basis) to the reduced submodule.
